h: Shemittah Renews the Divine Purpose Within the Years of Work

p: "And the land shall rest a Shabbos unto Hashem.
Six years you shall sow your field, etc.
there shall be a Shabbos of rest for the land,
just as is said of the Shabbos of Creation";
to the wording of the Toras Kohanim
The Ramban, of blessed memory, already asked
must have the intent of being for the sake of Hashem.
נִדְרָשׁ זֶה עַל שַׁבָּת לַה׳ הַשֵּׁנִי
this is expounded on the second "a Shabbos unto Hashem."
The point is that there is a difficulty in the verse,
where it is written, "And the land shall rest a Shabbos unto Hashem":
that it refers to the mitzvah of Shemittah,
Also, the wording of the verse,
surely upon their entry into Eretz Yisrael
for after seven years in which they conquered
and seven in which they divided the land,
This is what troubled the Toras Kohanim,
and that is why it expounded "a Shabbos unto Hashem
just as is said of the Shabbos of Creation."
For it says in the Gemara (Shabbos 69b):
like the creation of the world;
and afterward, on the sixth day,
came the corruption of the serpent,
and Shabbos was given to Adam HaRishon
so that he could repair the corruption;
so that through the holiness of Shabbos
he could repair the days of work,
to make the repair on Shabbos properly,
there would have been then the world of repair,
as it will be in the future.
And at the Giving of the Torah,
that they would not have died
which is the Angel of Death
in the manner of what they said
(in the She'iltos, cited in Tanchuma Bereishis):
just as I rested on it";
that is, that there would be
during the six days of work
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
it is written in the second Tablets (Devarim 5:15):
"And you shall remember that you were a slave, etc.,
to make the day of Shabbos";
that is, that the holiness should be
And this is why Shabbos is called
and this is "a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt"
So too the verse says here,
that at the very beginning of Yisrael's entry
"the land shall rest a Shabbos unto Hashem":
that it should always be like Shabbasos,
as at the beginning of Creation:
"and I was created to serve my Maker"
and their work is done by others;
and as at the Giving of the Torah:
"Six years you shall sow your field, etc.,
do the will of the Omnipresent,
their work is done by themselves,
'And you shall gather in your grain.'"
for this is written in the passage
"And it will be, if you hearken, etc."
that certainly the command of the Omnipresent is
to engage in work six days
and one must also toil at work,
But the will of the Omnipresent
at the beginning of Creation was
that man be free only for Torah,
וְאָז מְלַאכְתָּן נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
and then their work is done by others,
as it will be in the future.
And this is what it says:
אָז מְלַאכְתָּן נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי עַצְמָן
then their work is done by themselves:
"and you shall gather in your grain"
And this is what is said here:
that is, when they do not do
And this is what is said:
there shall be a Shabbos of rest for the land."
like "ishon, the apple of the eye"
that is, just as on Shabbos
there is a holiness fixed and established
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach
so too in Shemittah as well
there is holiness from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
by fulfilling the mitzvah of Shemittah.
And this is what is said: "a Shabbos unto Hashem,"
as is said of the Shabbos of Creation.
That is, as with Adam HaRishon,
who had the day of Shabbos,
וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, ה)
"And strangers shall stand and tend your flocks" (Yeshayahu 61:5);
and at any rate it helped
to bring holiness into the days of work,
immediately "the land shall rest a Shabbos unto Hashem";
they would all have been free only for Torah,
and their work would be done by others,
as it will be in the future:
in a manner where one must toil at work;
there shall be a Shabbos of rest for the land"
this is holiness from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
and from the side of man,
as with the Shabbos of Creation.
